title: Perforce
text:
Perforce was founded in 1995 in Alameda, California by Christopher Seiwald, a software developer and computer science graduate from UC Berkeley.[1] Its first product was also called Perforce, and was a version control system allowing companies to collaborate on large software projects by keeping track of changes to both the source code and binary files.[1,2]

In June 2013, the company released P4 Code Review (formerly Helix Swarm), a tool for developers working in different geographic areas to collaborate on code review.[3]

In June 2014, the company released a version of its Perforce versioning engine, then known as P4D, which supported concurrency.[4]

In March 2015, the company renamed its product to Perforce Helix, which now supported distributed development and included security features allowing suspicious usage tracking.[5] Helix's security capabilities included IP threat detection, co-developed with analytics vendor Interset.[6] In October, the company collaborated with GitLab to release GitSwarm, a software tool that combined git distributed workflow for developers with Perforce's single code repository.[7]

In February 2016, Seiwald sold the company to investment group Summit Partners, and Janet Dryer was named as new CEO.[8] The company headquarters was relocated to Minneapolis.[9] In November, Perforce announced the acquisition of Seapine Software, a provider of application lifecycle management (ALM) tools.[10] Seapine's TestTrack ALM software was rebranded as Helix ALM and eventually Perforce ALM.[11]

In September 2017, the company acquired Uppsala, Sweden-based Hansoft, a developer of Agile planning software.[12] Also in September, Perforce announced it had acquired Finnish repository management services company Deveo.[13] Deveo's products were merged into Perforce TeamHub, its first solo venture for Git-based development teams.

In January 2018, Summit Partners sold Perforce to private equity firm Clearlake Capital.[14] In May, Perforce acquired UK-based Programming Research (PRQA), a static code analysis firm.[15] In June, the company announced that CEO Janet Dryer was moving to the role of Chair of the Board, and COO/CFO Mark Ties was taking the role of CEO.[16] In October, the company acquired mobile and web automation testing company Perfecto.[17]

In January 2019, Perforce announced the acquisition of Rogue Wave Software, a software company with a focus on development tools for high-performance computing.[18] In April, private equity firm Francisco Partners acquired 50% of Perforce, becoming an equal partner with Clearlake Capital.[19] In September, Perforce Software was awarded the 2019 Computer Entertainment Developers Conference (CEDEC) Award for Engineering for P4 (formerly Helix Core).[20,21]

In June 2020, Perforce acquired software developer TestCraft Technologies, a provider of automated Selenium-based web application testing.[22] In July, Perforce acquired software developer Methodics, a DevOps software provider of intellectual property life cycle management for semiconductor companies.[23]

In October 2021, Perforce agreed to buy BlazeMeter testing platform from Broadcom Inc for an undisclosed sum.[24]

In April 2022, Perforce acquired the Portland, Oregon-based infrastructure automation software platform, Puppet.[25,26]

In March 2024, Perforce acquired the Redwood City, California-based test data management software, Delphix.[27]
